title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 12.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Rehoboam forsook the law of the LORD
Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem
Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam
The princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam forsook the law of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:1 states that after Rehoboam established the kingdom and strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the LORD, which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who came up against Jerusalem in the fifth year of King Rehoboam?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:2 says that in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

questions.question: Why did Shishak king of Egypt come up against Jerusalem?
options: Because they had transgressed against the LORD
To take control of Judah's gold
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had transgressed against the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:2 explains that Shishak came against Jerusalem because they had transgressed against the LORD.

questions.question: How many chariots did Shishak bring when he came against Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:3 states that Shishak came with twelve hundred chariots.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 12, how many horsemen came with Shishak from Egypt?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:3 mentions that Shishak came with threescore thousand horsemen, which is sixty thousand.

questions.question: Which groups of people came with Shishak out of Egypt?
options: The Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians
The Philistines, the Moabites, and the Ammonites
The Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Jebusites
The Assyrians, the Babylonians, and the Medes
questions.correctAnswer: The Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:3 lists the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians as the peoples who came with Shishak from Egypt.

questions.question: What did Shishak take when he came against Judah?
options: The fenced cities which pertained to Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The fenced cities which pertained to Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:4 says that Shishak took the fenced cities which pertained to Judah.

questions.question: Who came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah because of Shishak's invasion?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:5 states that Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah due to Shishak's invasion.

questions.question: What message did Shemaiah the prophet deliver to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah?
options: "Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak."
"The LORD will protect you if you repent."
questions.correctAnswer: "Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak."
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:5 records Shemaiah's message that they have forsaken the LORD and therefore He has left them in the hand of Shishak.

questions.question: How did the princes of Israel and the king respond after Shemaiah's message?
options: They humbled themselves and said, The LORD is righteous.
They planned to fight Shishak immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: They humbled themselves and said, The LORD is righteous.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:6 states that the princes and the king humbled themselves and acknowledged the LORD's righteousness.

questions.question: Who strengthened himself after establishing the kingdom according to 2 Chronicles 12?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:1 says that Rehoboam had established the kingdom and strengthened himself.

questions.question: True or False: Shishak king of Egypt brought more than one thousand chariots when he came against Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:3 states Shishak came with twelve hundred chariots, which is more than one thousand.

questions.question: True or False: The people who came with Shishak out of Egypt included the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:3 lists the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians as accompanying Shishak from Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that Rehoboam built new cities to defend Judah against Shishak.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12 does not mention Rehoboam building new cities; rather, Shishak took the fenced cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 12:4).

questions.question: True or False: Shemaiah told Rehoboam that the LORD would send a plague upon Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:5 records that Shemaiah said they forsook the LORD and were left in the hand of Shishak, but does not mention a plague.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise when He saw that they humbled themselves?
options: I will grant them some deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: I will grant them some deliverance
questions.explanation: The LORD promised deliverance because they humbled themselves as stated in 2 Chronicles 12:7.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 12:8 promise will happen if someone serves the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:8 indicates that serving the LORD leads to understanding His service.

questions.question: What did Shishak take from Jerusalem?
options: The treasures of the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The treasures of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Shishak took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house according to 2 Chronicles 12:9.

questions.question: What did Rehoboam make instead of gold shields?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam made shields of brass as stated in 2 Chronicles 12:10.

questions.question: What happened when the king entered the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: When the king entered the house of the LORD, the guard fetched the shields and brought them back into the guard chamber as per 2 Chronicles 12:11.

questions.question: What was the outcome after Rehoboam humbled himself?
options: The wrath of the LORD turned from him
questions.correctAnswer: The wrath of the LORD turned from him
questions.explanation: After Rehoboam humbled himself, the wrath of the LORD turned from him, which is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 12:12.

questions.question: How did the princes of Israel respond to Shemaiah's message?
questions.explanation: The princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves in response to the message from Shemaiah as stated in 2 Chronicles 12:6.

questions.question: What can be learned about obedience from 2 Chronicles 12:5?
options: It can lead to surrender to enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to surrender to enemies
questions.explanation: The verse shows that forsaking the LORD leads to being left in the hand of Shishak, highlighting the consequences of disobedience in 2 Chronicles 12:5.

questions.question: What does the act of humbling oneself signify in a spiritual context?
questions.explanation: Humbling oneself signifies strength in faith and recognition of God's authority, which is evident in the positive response from the LORD when Rehoboam and the princes humbled themselves.

questions.question: In what way did Shishak's attack serve as a consequence?
options: It was an attack of opportunity
It was a sign of weakness
questions.explanation: Shishak's attack served as a consequence of Israel's transgression against the LORD, showcasing God's judgment as stated in 2 Chronicles 12:2.

questions.question: What does the story of Rehoboam remind us about leadership?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's experience illustrates the importance of relying on God rather than forsaking His law, as shown in 2 Chronicles 12:1.

questions.question: What is one lesson on humility from 2 Chronicles 12?
options: It is a sign of weakness
questions.explanation: The chapter demonstrates that humility before God can lead to deliverance and a turning away of His wrath, as seen in 2 Chronicles 12:7.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised to destroy Jerusalem after the people humbled themselves.
questions.explanation: The LORD promised not to destroy them after they humbled themselves, as stated in 2 Chronicles 12:7.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam's actions led to prosperity for Israel.
questions.explanation: Rehoboam forsook the law of the LORD, which led to his downfall and Shishak's attack, indicating that his actions did not lead to prosperity, as seen in 2 Chronicles 12:1.

questions.question: True or False: Shishak came against Jerusalem because the people were faithful to God.
questions.explanation: Shishak came against Jerusalem because the people had transgressed against the LORD, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 12:2.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 12.

questions.question: How old was King Rehoboam when he began to reign according to 2 Chronicles 12:13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:13 states that Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: Which city did Rehoboam reign in, as described in 2 Chronicles 12:13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:13 specifies that Rehoboam reigned in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD had chosen.

questions.question: What was the nationality of Rehoboam's mother Naamah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 12:13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:13 identifies Rehoboam's mother Naamah as an Ammonitess.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 12:14, why did Rehoboam do evil?
options: Because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD
Because he sought the LORD's enemies
Because he was influenced by Jeroboam
Because he was deceived by prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:14 explicitly says Rehoboam did evil because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.

questions.question: Where are the acts of Rehoboam recorded as referenced in 2 Chronicles 12:15?
options: In the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer
In the book of the Kings of Israel
In the scroll of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: In the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:15 states that Rehoboam's acts are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer.

questions.question: Who succeeded Rehoboam as king according to 2 Chronicles 12:16?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:16 records that Rehoboam was succeeded by his son Abijah.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'חָזַק' (chazaq) in 2 Chronicles 12:13 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'חָזַק' (chazaq) used in 2 Chronicles 12:13 means to strengthen or make firm, as in 'Rehoboam strengthened himself'.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the contrast between Rehoboam's initial strength and his evil deeds in 2 Chronicles 12:13-14?
questions.explanation: There is irony in 2 Chronicles 12:13-14 where Rehoboam is described as strengthening himself but then doing evil because he did not seek the LORD.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's judgment due to forsaking His law as seen in 2 Chronicles 12:1-2?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28:15 warns of consequences for forsaking the LORD's laws, connecting to 2 Chronicles 12:1-2 where Rehoboam and Israel forsook the law and faced judgment.

questions.question: The continual wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam mentioned in 2 Chronicles 12:15 echo which Old Testament narrative about divided kingdoms?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:20 describes the division of Israel and the rivalry between Jeroboam and Rehoboam, echoing the continual wars referenced in 2 Chronicles 12:15.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Rehoboam strengthening himself in Jerusalem, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 12?
options: The Lord's wrath turning away after Rehoboam humbled himself
The taking of treasures by Shishak
The building of shields of brass
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord's wrath turning away after Rehoboam humbled himself
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:12 records that when Rehoboam humbled himself, the Lord's wrath turned away, which immediately precedes his strengthening himself as described in 12:13.

questions.question: How does the account of Shishak's invasion in 2 Chronicles 12:2-9 serve as a typological foreshadowing in biblical history?
options: It foreshadows later invasions by Assyria and Babylon as judgment for sin
It is a type of Christ's victory over sin
It represents the Exodus from Egypt
It prefigures the establishment of the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows later invasions by Assyria and Babylon as judgment for sin
questions.explanation: Shishak's invasion in 2 Chronicles 12 illustrates God's judgment on Israel for sin, a pattern repeated with later Assyrian and Babylonian invasions, thus serving as typological foreshadowing.

questions.question: What is the significance of Rehoboam being buried in the city of David as noted in 2 Chronicles 12:16?
options: It symbolizes continuity with David's dynasty despite Rehoboam's failings
It indicates rejection by the people
It marks the end of Judah's monarchy
It shows he was not considered a legitimate king
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes continuity with David's dynasty despite Rehoboam's failings
questions.explanation: Burial in the city of David in 2 Chronicles 12:16 signifies royal legitimacy and continuity with David's dynasty despite Rehoboam's moral failings.

questions.question: Which thematic parallelism can be observed between Rehoboam’s reign described in 2 Chronicles 12 and the New Testament teaching about leadership in James 4:6?
options: God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth
The first shall be last, and the last shall be first
To whom much is given, much will be required
questions.correctAnswer: God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble
questions.explanation: Rehoboam’s initial pride and later humility (2 Chronicles 12:6-12) parallels James 4:6 teaching that God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 12:14, Rehoboam did evil because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:14 explicitly states that Rehoboam did evil because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 12:1 teach about human sin?
options: Sin involves forsaking the law of the LORD by both leader and people
Sin is primarily a failure to offer sacrifices
Sin is only individual and not corporate
Sin cannot be identified in political leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Sin involves forsaking the law of the LORD by both leader and people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:1 states that Rehoboam and all Israel forsook the law of the LORD, showing sin as a corporate abandonment of God's covenant law.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is communicated in 2 Chronicles 12:2?
options: God uses foreign nations as instruments of judgment for transgression
God directly inflicts punishment without intermediaries
God's judgment is always immediate and total
God's judgment is only spiritual and never physical
questions.correctAnswer: God uses foreign nations as instruments of judgment for transgression
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:2 shows that Shishak king of Egypt came against Jerusalem because Israel had transgressed against the LORD, illustrating God’s use of nations to execute judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning prophetic mediation is evident in 2 Chronicles 12:5?
options: Prophets serve as God's mouthpiece to call people to repentance
Prophets only predict the future without calling for repentance
Prophets primarily support the king without rebuke
Prophets reveal hidden mysteries unrelated to covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets serve as God's mouthpiece to call people to repentance
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:5 records Shemaiah the prophet declaring God’s word to Rehoboam and the princes, calling them to recognize their forsaking of God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 12:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows God’s patience as He refrains from destroying Jerusalem after the people humbled themselves, demonstrating His longsuffering nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 12:6?
questions.explanation: The princes acknowledge that 'The LORD is righteous' in verse 6, highlighting God’s attribute of perfect justice.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 12:9 connect to the broader biblical theme of the consequences of idolatry?
options: The removal of the temple treasures illustrates loss of divine blessing due to unfaithfulness
It shows God rewarding Israel with wealth
It indicates that temples should be fortified militarily
It emphasizes the importance of human strength over divine protection
questions.correctAnswer: The removal of the temple treasures illustrates loss of divine blessing due to unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 9 describes Shishak taking away the treasures of the LORD’s house, symbolizing the loss Israel experienced because of their idolatry and disobedience.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is prefigured in 2 Chronicles 12:12 regarding divine discipline and restoration?
options: God’s wrath turning away after humility foreshadows Christ’s intercessory role
The passage predicts Israel’s permanent exile without hope
It teaches that repentance has no effect on divine judgment
It denies any future restoration for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath turning away after humility foreshadows Christ’s intercessory role
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows that when Rehoboam humbled himself, God relented from destroying Judah, prefiguring Christ’s saving intercession to turn away God’s wrath (cf. 1 John 2:1-2).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 12:6 and 2 Chronicles 12:7 teach about repentance and divine response?
options: True humility leads God to withhold deserved judgment
Repentance has no influence on God’s decrees
God’s wrath is unchangeable regardless of human action
Humility is irrelevant to covenant relationship
questions.correctAnswer: True humility leads God to withhold deserved judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together teach that when the leaders humbled themselves and acknowledged God's righteousness, the Lord chose not to destroy them, showing repentance’s power to avert judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 12:1 and 2 Chronicles 12:14 teach about the heart’s orientation and evil actions?
options: Preparing the heart to seek the LORD is necessary to avoid doing evil
One can do evil and yet have a prepared heart
Rehoboam's evil was unrelated to his heart condition
questions.correctAnswer: Preparing the heart to seek the LORD is necessary to avoid doing evil
questions.explanation: Verse 1 notes forsaking God’s law while verse 14 observes Rehoboam did evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD, linking heart disposition with moral conduct.

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Chronicles 12:2 and 2 Chronicles 12:8 offer about servitude and divine purpose?
options: God allows servitude under foreign powers to teach His people about true service
Servitude is always a sign of divine rejection without purpose
God’s people are never subjected to foreign rule
Servitude is a permanent curse without redemptive meaning
questions.correctAnswer: God allows servitude under foreign powers to teach His people about true service
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows Shishak attacking due to transgression, and verse 8 says they shall be servants to know God’s service, teaching servitude as corrective discipline.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 12:5-8 teaches God’s abandonment of His people without mercy. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God disciplines but shows mercy by withholding total destruction when people humble themselves
God abandons His people completely with no hope of restoration
God’s judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to human repentance
The passage promotes despair rather than hope
questions.correctAnswer: God disciplines but shows mercy by withholding total destruction when people humble themselves
questions.explanation: Verses 5-8 explain that though God handed them over to Shishak due to sin, He refrained from destroying Jerusalem because they humbled themselves, showing merciful discipline.

questions.question: What doctrine about the sufficiency of divine protection versus human means is taught in 2 Chronicles 12:10-11?
options: Human substitutes (bronze shields) cannot replace God’s original provision (gold shields)
Human effort is always sufficient for security
Divine protection is unnecessary when human guards are present
questions.correctAnswer: Human substitutes (bronze shields) cannot replace God’s original provision (gold shields)
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 describe Rehoboam replacing gold shields taken by Shishak with bronze ones, symbolizing a diminished protection compared to God’s original blessing through Solomon’s gold shields.

questions.question: What doctrine of covenant election and divine choice is taught in 2 Chronicles 12:13?
options: God’s sovereign choice of Jerusalem as the city to place His name affirms His covenant faithfulness
The city of Jerusalem was chosen by human decision alone
God’s election is based on human merit
The Lord’s name is placed in many cities equally
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign choice of Jerusalem as the city to place His name affirms His covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states Jerusalem was the city the LORD chose to put His name there, emphasizing divine election and faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly manifested in 2 Chronicles 12:4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows Shishak capturing cities and coming to Jerusalem, demonstrating God’s sovereign control over nations and events as instruments of His will.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do 2 Chronicles 12:15 and 2 Chronicles 12:16 provide about the nature of kingship and covenant continuity?
options: Despite ongoing conflicts, the Davidic covenant line continues unbroken
Kingship is unstable and not divinely sanctioned
Genealogies are irrelevant to covenant promises
The covenant is nullified with each king’s death
questions.correctAnswer: Despite ongoing conflicts, the Davidic covenant line continues unbroken
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 show the ongoing wars and Rehoboam’s death but affirm his burial in the city of David and succession by his son, underscoring covenant continuity.
